It is review-only and records codex_model, codex_effort and codex_usage as null. judgments.why:
Return A's winner set {c12, c7} is better supported than Return B's {c12, c7, c11}. Both sets share c12 and c7, and the evidence supports both.

- c12: blueprints/convergence-practice/native-worker/README.md lines 8-14 shows a native child that repaired only planner.py in its own worktree. All 12 unchanged tests passed and the primary checkout stayed clean.
- c7: catalogs/foundation/decisions.json lines 478-499 records owned-worktrees as selection 'default' with status accepted_within_scope. Create/list/remove passed, and a dirty removal was refused without losing work.

B's only extra component is c11 (Codex native workers), and nothing retained shows it delegating owned edits.
- decisions.json line 2678 says 'Codex agent examples inherit model and effort and have no end-to-end run of their own'.
- agent-sdk-runtime-selection (decisions.json lines 2831-2841) is conditional and source_review, and 'no new execution was run'.
- B's Codex execution evidence, evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/native-review.json, is a companion /codex:review run. That is the c8 plugin path, and it only reviews. It returned 'No actionable regressions were found' with codex_model, codex_effort and codex_usage all null.
- docs/foundation-rd-readiness.md lines 53-55 likewise shows Codex only as an independent reviewer.

So Codex covers the review part of the requirement but not bounded delegation or preservation of owned edits and failed results. B adds a component the evidence does not support. Neither return makes a claim the evidence contradicts, so 'neither' does not apply.

The two returns differ on one component only: Codex native workers (c11). A includes it and B does not. The layer requirement has three parts: delegate bounded work, keep owned edits and actual failed results, and integrate only after review. For Codex, the retained evidence covers only the review part, and that part comes through a different component.

- **The review evidence belongs to the companion (c8).** evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/native-review.json records a literal Claude `/codex:review` call through the official companion (codex-plugin-cc 1.0.6, at the pin recorded in the packet). The file reports "No actionable regressions were found" and `review_checkout_unchanged: true`. That run belongs to c8, which A itself lists only as conditional. The same file sets `codex_model`, `codex_effort` and `codex_usage` to null.
- **No owned Codex writing child is recorded.** docs/foundation-rd-readiness.md lines 53-55 and 136-137 record only an independent native Codex review of a three-file guard correction.
- **Codex's worker-layer decision covers session resume only.** In catalogs/foundation/decisions.json, native-session-resume (lines 1950-1981) is "conditional". It records that Codex on Mac resumed one unchanged checkpoint, and says this "does not establish arbitrary worker crash, provider cancellation or whole-host recovery".
- **Codex worker examples were never run.** decisions.json line 2678 says the "Codex agent examples inherit model and effort and have no end-to-end run of their own".
- **The retained-failure evidence is Claude-only.** docs/native-workflow-writing-recovery-20260921.md lines 95-121 record a stopped reviewer kept as a failed child with `review: null`, then replay and review-gated integration. Every run there is a Claude Workflow run.

So c11 does not meet the delegation, ownership and failure-retention parts at least as well as Claude native workers (c12), and A's own open gaps concede this. The shared winners, c12 and Worktrunk (c7), are the same in both returns and supported in both. B's set is therefore better supported. Adding c11 does not contradict the evidence, which is why "neither" does not apply.
